subject: Pipeline rate-limit exception: temporary derate & customer notification
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: [Incident] FastCart p99 jump in gen-api (regional)

Team —

Observing a sustained p99 latency increase for FastCart's gen-api traffic starting ~07:40 PT. Traffic is concentrated in us-west-2 and correlates with increased request fanout on the mapping pipeline. Current facts:

- P99 for gen-api endpoints rose from ~230ms to ~1.8s for ~60m.
- Throughput overall held but we see higher token-level CPU pressure on the multi-tenant pools serving the customer.
- Autoscale did not add capacity due to a rate-limit rule on the pool (configured for steady-state guarantees).

I'll paste a short snippet of the live graph and the incident log in the follow-up. Early hypothesis: rate-limit/derate policy prevented autoscale bump for this account leading to queuing.

Immediate asks:
1) Eng/SRE: can we temporarily lift the rate-limit/derate for FastCart to allow additional pods and reduce queuing?
2) Product: we need a short customer-facing message (2–3 lines) that explains we're applying a configuration change to restore performance and will follow up with root cause.

I'm pausing any forced rollouts in the region until we stabilize.

Thanks,
Jonas

[attachment: grafana-fastcart-p99-20261119.png]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T08:29:00-08:00
Subject: Re: [Incident] FastCart p99 jump in gen-api (regional)

Thanks Jonas — good catch.

Ben/Diego: please proceed with the minimal change to allow autoscale to add capacity for FastCart in us-west-2. Specifically: remove the per-account derate cap for FC-3482 for the next 2 hours and monitor queue length. Keep everything else intact.

Marissa: can you draft the customer note below? Short, actionable, no technical blame: say we applied a temporary configuration change to improve performance and we will send a postmortem within 48 hours. I'll approve the language before it goes out.

Jonas: assign an incident owner and create the Jira OPS-9123 with initial findings and timeline. Include the logs attachment.

Soojin

On it — will do the derate lift now and keep it scoped to FC-3482. Action plan:

1) Remove derate cap for FC-3482 and trigger a scale check (target +2 pods). ETA: 6m.
2) Watch token CPU, queue depth, and latency across p50/p90/p99.
3) If we see regression, fall back to original config and notify you immediately.

"Emily — we observed a temporary performance degradation affecting a subset of requests in us-west-2. We've applied a configuration change to restore normal response times and are monitoring closely. We'll follow up with a detailed update and timeline within 48 hours. Apologies for the disruption. — Soojin on behalf of Redwood Inference Ops"

Posting the incident log and an output of the scale command to Jira after the change.

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: [Incident] FastCart p99 jump in gen-api (regional)

Update after derate lift:

- We removed the per-account derate and scale target increased by 2 pods within ~4m. P99 dropped from 1.8s -> 320ms within ~9m of the change.
- Root cause trace: a malformed customer traffic pattern caused an atypical token fanout in the embedding-mapper stage; multi-tenant kernel scheduling amplified latency under the previous cap. Not a code regression in serving runtime, more a workload edge-case interacting with the rate-limit guardrail.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Keep derate lifted for another 1 hour while we capture traces and a representative sample.
2) Eng (Jonas + Diego) to build a short-term scheduling tweak that reduces token-level preemption for multi-tenant pools (target: mitigate map-stage fanout impact). ETA: 3 days for a canary patch.
3) Product/PD: consider a configuration knob that allows us to grant temporary burst capacity to enterprise accounts without manual intervention — roadmap ask.

I'll attach the filtered traces and the timeline to OPS-9123.

Diego

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Emily Wong <emily.wong@fastcart.com>, Kyle Park <kyle.park@fastcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T13:45:00-08:00
Subject: Incident update: action taken to restore performance for FastCart (us-west-2)

Emily / Kyle —

Thanks again for flagging the latency issues this morning. Quick update from the Redwood Ops team: 

- What happened: A specific request pattern triggered increased internal fanout which interacted with a per-account rate guard, causing elevated p99 latency for a subset of gen-api calls in us-west-2.
- What we did: We removed the per-account derate cap and allowed autoscale to add capacity; this reduced p99 from ~1.8s to ~320ms within ~10 minutes.
- Current status: Performance has returned to expected ranges; we're monitoring closely for 60 more minutes.
- Next steps: We'll deliver a technical postmortem within 48 hours outlining root cause, mitigation, and a path to prevent recurrence (short-term scheduling tweak and a product configuration for burst capacity).

If you'd like a quick call to walk through the timeline and what to expect in the postmortem, I'm available after 15:00 PT today.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll follow up with a detailed write-up.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
